crossfade_model.note: naive linear 0.25 s CURRENT crossfade (no flux forcing) in the two-mode RFOC model: the terminal voltage follows the rotor flux, which lags the current by tau_r (0.48 s for 2p8, 1.46 s for 2p4), so V8 stays high while I4 rises and the envelope factor exceeds 1. The ideal x(1-x) = 0.25 assumes the fluxes track the currents instantly. The true factor of a flux-forced overlapped schedule lies between; the simulator's MEC run (confirm_H10) decides.

sequential_V8_I4_term.note: 'sequential' = drop all 2p8 current, then build 2p4 under the pulsation limit; the decaying 2p8 rotor flux still induces V8, so 3 V8 I4 limits the 2p4 build current until the flux has decayed

balancing_knob_correction.statement: The power shift per ampere of a same-frequency balancing order b is m V_p (main-mode leg voltage x m), independent of the winding factor of b. Signed orders count: for p = 4, m = 5 the order b = -1 (counter-rotating 2-pole) satisfies 5 | (p - b). So m = 5 is NOT a weaker knob (H10 said so - corrected).

H11s.target: +-10 % ripple at 2.9 mF, torque gap <= 0.2 s, no torque reversal, flat and 2 % grade, 2100 rpm
H11s.schedule: A: ramp 2p8 torque current to 0 in 20 ms; B: demagnetise 2p8 with i_d8 = -I_max until psi8 < 2 % (single order -> no cell pulsation); C: build 2p4 flux with i_d4 up to the current budget, 2p4 current limited online by 3 (V8 I4 + V4 I8) <= P_allow(f8+f4, C, ripple); torque current as soon as psi4 > 5 %; D: run
H11s.model_note: Two-mode RFOC model with T03 IM parameters at 300 kW (I_max 266 A); linear magnetics (no saturation intermodulation); simulator confirm_H10 (MEC) should repeat it.

post_bypass_mode_table.note: Bypass = module DC port shorted, its coil group unpowered (fixed wiring; at N = 15 c = Q/(mN) is not an integer, so the remaining coils cannot be regrouped - the machine runs with a hole). Cell voltage limit 0.80 V_class (H05).

unit_cost_assumptions.note: Unit prices are assumed order-of-magnitude distributor list prices at ~1k pcs, NOT verified (no web access in this run). Request lit-scout/Enes to replace with quotes. Ratios matter more than absolutes.

hybrid_polymer_100V_330uF.size: 12.5 x 20 mm (typical); ripple rating at low frequency is much lower than at 100 kHz

MLCC_100V_22uF_X7S_2220.size: TDK C5750X7S2A226M280KB as on Rev B; 0.35 DC-bias retention assumed

unit_cost_assumptions.life_target_note: truck: ~1.2 Mkm at ~50 km/h average -> ~25 kh operating (assumption)

a_IM_transient_H11s.note: pulsation-constrained schedule needs no extra capacitance if H11s meets the target (see H11s)

c_post_bypass_N_minus_1.note: No cell pulsation or average imbalance from the hole in either m (first order); both lose 1/16 of the fundamental. Two bypassed cells exceed 0.80 V_class (85.7 V on 100 V) for both. m = 5 gives no post-bypass advantage.

cost_table.verdict: m = 5 does not win a steady-state case clearly: (b) continuous excitation is cheaper as m = 3 + bulk capacitance than as 32 extra legs (+winding), and (c) post-bypass gives no m = 5 advantage. m = 5 keeps the advantage of zero extra C and no electrolytic lifetime limit in (b).
